description: Regime-keyed recommendation templates. The dashboard selects a regime from the selected product's expected price change, then formats the body with live numbers. Placeholders: product, unit, currency, current, forecast, lower, upper, change, horizon, date, model, volatility, risk, saving.

rising_sharp.title: Release buffer stocks now
rising_sharp.body: A {change:+.1f}% move in {product} over {horizon} days hits low-income households directly. Trigger open-market sales through TCB outlets in the districts with the thinnest supply before the projected peak on {date}.

rising_sharp.title: Fast-track import clearance
rising_sharp.body: Waive or reduce duty and clear consignments of {product} within days rather than weeks. Import lead time is the binding constraint when the projected peak is only {horizon} days out.

rising_sharp.title: Publish a weekly price bulletin
rising_sharp.body: Announce the projected band of {lower:,.0f}–{upper:,.0f} {unit} publicly. Transparent official forecasts reduce the speculative hoarding that drives a large part of short-run retail spikes.

rising.title: Put buffer stocks on standby
rising.body: The {model} model points to a {change:+.1f}% rise in {product} by {date}. Confirm warehouse positions now so an intervention can be executed within a week if realised prices track the upper band of {upper:,.0f} {unit}.

rising.title: Monitor wholesale-to-retail margins
rising.body: Moderate upward pressure is where margin widening hides. Compare wholesale and bazaar prices for {product} weekly across the {horizon}-day window and publish the gap.

rising.title: Pre-position social protection
rising.body: Confirm OMS and VGF distribution lists now. A {change:+.1f}% rise is absorbable for most households but not for the bottom two income deciles.

stable.title: Use the window to rebuild stocks
stable.body: {product} is projected to stay within {change:+.1f}% of today's {current:,.2f} {unit}. A flat market is the cheapest moment to replenish public buffer stocks ahead of the next lean season.

stable.title: Hold interventions in reserve
stable.body: No price action is warranted while the forecast band stays inside {lower:,.0f}–{upper:,.0f} {unit}. Preserve fiscal space for the commodities that are actually moving.

stable.title: Invest in the data pipeline
stable.body: Quiet periods are when monitoring systems should be improved. Extending daily price collection to more upazilas raises forecast quality for the next shock at almost no political cost.

falling.title: Protect farm-gate prices
falling.body: A projected {change:+.1f}% decline in {product} helps consumers but squeezes growers. Consider procurement at a floor price so the correction does not depress next season's planting decisions.

falling.title: Expand cold-storage access
falling.body: Cheap {product} is only useful if it can be held. Subsidised storage during the {horizon}-day soft patch smooths the following peak far more cheaply than emergency imports do.

falling.title: Build the public stock now
falling.body: Procuring into the buffer at {forecast:,.2f} {unit} rather than at a crisis price is the single highest-return action available in a falling market.

rising_sharp.title: Buy ahead of the peak
rising_sharp.body: {product} is projected to reach {forecast:,.2f} {unit} by {date}, up {change:+.1f}% from {current:,.2f}. If it stores well, buying now avoids roughly {saving:,.0f} {currency} on a month of typical household use.

rising_sharp.title: Substitute where you can
rising_sharp.body: During a sharp {product} run-up, shifting part of the basket to items forecast to stay flat protects the food budget without cutting the number of meals.

rising_sharp.title: Buy in bulk with neighbours
rising_sharp.body: Wholesale rates are typically 8–15% below retail. Pooling a single sack of {product} across households captures that gap exactly when the retail price is climbing.

rising.title: Stagger your purchases
rising.body: With a {change:+.1f}% rise expected by {date}, buying in two or three tranches over the next {horizon} days beats one large purchase — you average into the move instead of trying to time it.

rising.title: Plan against the upper band
rising.body: The 95% interval for {product} reaches {upper:,.0f} {unit}. Treat that, not the central forecast, as the worst case when setting a monthly food budget.

stable.title: No need to stockpile
stable.body: {product} is expected to stay near {forecast:,.2f} {unit} through {date}. Normal weekly buying is the cheapest strategy; stockpiling only adds spoilage risk.

stable.title: Compare outlets instead
stable.body: When the market is flat, the spread between bazaars is larger than the spread over time. Shopping around beats timing the purchase.

falling.title: Wait before bulk buying
falling.body: {product} is projected to ease to {forecast:,.2f} {unit} by {date} ({change:+.1f}%). Deferring a bulk purchase by a few weeks saves about {saving:,.0f} {currency} on a month of typical use.

falling.title: Good moment to preserve
falling.body: A soft patch in {product} is the right time to buy for drying, pickling or freezing if your household does that.

Onion.policy: Onion price shocks in Bangladesh are historically import-policy events. Coordinate with the Ministry of Commerce on alternative sourcing (Türkiye, Egypt, China) before the domestic lean season, not during it.
Onion.consumer: Onion stores well in a dry, ventilated place for several weeks, so it is one of the few basket items where buying ahead of a forecast spike genuinely pays.

Potato.policy: Cold-storage capacity and release timing are the effective policy levers for potato. Monitor storage occupancy alongside price — a full store with rising prices signals withholding, not scarcity.
Potato.consumer: Potato keeps for months in a cool dark place, so bulk buying during a projected soft patch is low-risk for most households.

Soybean Oil.policy: Because soybean oil is import-dependent, duty adjustments and letter-of-credit facilitation act faster than stock releases. Watch the exchange rate as a leading indicator of the retail price.
Soybean Oil.consumer: Bottled soybean oil has a long shelf life, so buying an extra month's supply ahead of a projected rise carries almost no spoilage risk.
